title: Deep Learning Primer for Systems Engineers

content.value: Primary reading: Machine Learning Systems, Chapter 3. Supplemental: open deep learning notes and framework tutorials for tensors, gradients, and inference pipelines.

This unit reviews deep learning from a systems perspective. The emphasis is not deriving every training rule from scratch, but understanding what computations happen, where memory is consumed, why batching matters, and how training and inference pipelines differ. Students connect tensors, layers, loss functions, gradients, optimizers, activations, preprocessing, and postprocessing to concrete system costs such as memory bandwidth, compute utilization, numerical precision, and data movement.
Supplemental sources for this unit are listed in the references below. Use them to compare the textbook framing with public talks, documentation, papers, and production guidance.
Studio: trace a small image classifier through preprocessing, forward pass, loss, backward pass, update, and inference. Deliverable: annotate each step with its main compute and memory pressure.

concepts.name: Neural network
concepts.description: A model made of connected layers of learned parameters that transform inputs into outputs.

concepts.name: Tensor
concepts.description: A multidimensional array used to represent data and model parameters in deep learning systems.

concepts.name: Activation function
concepts.description: A function applied inside a neural network layer to introduce nonlinearity.

concepts.name: Loss function
concepts.description: A function that measures how far model outputs are from desired targets during training.

concepts.name: Backpropagation
concepts.description: The algorithm for computing gradients through a neural network so parameters can be updated.

concepts.name: Gradient descent
concepts.description: An optimization method that updates parameters in the direction that reduces loss.

concepts.name: Epoch
concepts.description: One complete pass through the training dataset during model training.

concepts.name: Batch size
concepts.description: The number of training examples processed together in one training step.
